subject: Signature Encyclopedia

records.title: Stars
records.text: Stars are bodies of gas in the sky that give off light and heat. They look small because they are far away.

records.title: Rivers
records.text: Rivers are streams of water that flow across land toward a sea or a lake. They carry water, soil, and life along their course.

records.title: Numbers
records.text: Numbers are signs used for counting, measuring, and ordering things. Arithmetic is the study of how numbers combine.

records.title: Music
records.text: Music is sound arranged in rhythm and tune. It is made with voices and instruments and is heard in songs.

records.title: Bridges
records.text: Bridges are structures that carry a road or a path across a river, a valley, or another road.

records.title: Birds
records.text: Birds are animals with feathers and wings. Most birds can fly, and all birds lay eggs.

records.title: Bread
records.text: Bread is food made from dough, usually of wheat flour, water, and yeast, baked in an oven.

records.title: Maps
records.text: Maps are drawings that show places, roads, rivers, and land, so a reader can find the way.

records.title: Ships
records.text: Ships are large boats that carry people and goods across seas and rivers, moved by sails or engines.

records.title: Mountains
records.text: Mountains are high parts of the land, built from rock, often capped with snow at their tops.

records.title: Rain
records.text: Rain is water that falls from clouds when the drops grow heavy enough to fall.

records.title: Clocks
records.text: Clocks are tools that show the time. They count hours and minutes with hands, numbers, or a screen.

records.title: Mirror section: Description and history
records.text: Section 1 Description and history Signature Encyclopedia is a mirror of the encyclopedia kind of website: a website whose job is to explain subjects in articles, each article linked to related articles, so a reader can learn one subject and follow the links to the next. The encyclopedia kind of website began as printed books of articles arranged by subject, then as sets of volumes, and then as websites where every article links to others. This mirror follows that same shape: a search box, articles in plain words, and links between them. What this mirror holds is the network's own material. Its

records.title: Mirror section: Math proof (standard math + metamath)
records.text: Section 2 Math proof (standard math + metamath) The mirror's lookup rule is a deterministic scoring function. For a query Q of words q1 … qn and an article A with a title and keywords, the score is: score(Q, A) = 3 × (number of query words appearing in A's title) + 1 × (number of query words appearing in A's keywords) An article appears in the results only if every query word appears in its title or its keywords. Results are ordered by score, highest first; ties are broken alphabetically by title, so the order is the same every time for the same query. Worked example: the query "stars" against

records.title: Mirror section: Science proof
records.text: Section 3 Science proof The science behind this mirror is how knowledge is organized: an encyclopedia groups what is known into articles, one per subject, and links articles that share ideas. A reader who opens one article can follow the links to nearby subjects. The mirror uses the simplest honest form of that idea: a fixed sample set of articles, each carrying a title, keywords, and a short summary, with a search that scores titles above keywords. records.title: Mirror section: Spec / patent + 3D-print version
records.text: Section 5 Spec / patent + 3D-print version Spec. The Signature spec for this mirror is a draft specification for an encyclopedia mirror over a fixed, network-owned article set: the article format (title, keywords, summary), the scoring rule from Section 2, the result-order rule, and the no-tracking, no-account design. The spec is a draft — ready to file, not filed, not a granted patent. 3D-print version. An encyclopedia mirror is software: it has no physical form, so there is no 3D-print version of it. The mirror says so plainly rather than inventing one.

records.title: Mirror section: Demonstration programs / working prototypes
records.text: Section 6 Demonstration programs / working prototypes The demonstration on the page is the article search itself. Type a subject, press Search articles, and the mirror scores its sample set and shows the matching articles with their scores and summaries. Expected output for the query "stars": one article, "Stars", score 4 — 3 points for the title and 1 point for the keywords — with its summary about stars being bodies of gas in the sky that give off light and heat. The program runs entirely in the browser, on the sample set shipped in the page. Nothing is sent anywhere.

records.title: Mirror section: Two AIs
records.text: Section 7 Two AIs 1. The Signature Encyclopedia website AI The website AI of this mirror. It discusses the mirror, helps a reader find and follow articles in the field, explains any result and why it ranked where it did, and routes detailed questions to the website or database AI that owns the subject. 2. The AI version of the encyclopedia An AI version of the encyclopedia itself. It answers questions about subjects from the mirror's own article set, names the articles it used, and says plainly when a subject is not in its set. records.title: Mirror section: USE section — use, download, copy
records.text: Section 8 USE section — use, download, copy Use it: use the search box at the top of this page. Type a subject, press Search articles, and open any result. The search runs in your browser, on the sample set in the page. Download it: its page, its sample set, its spec, and both AIs with their specs are downloadable from this section, free forever. Copy it: the scoring rule in Section 2 is short enough to copy by hand: 3 points for a word in the title, 1 point for a word in the keywords, every query word must match, highest score first, ties alphabetical. records.title: Mirror section: Sources, codes, and network
records.text: Section 9 Sources, codes, and network Sources. The mirror's articles come from the network's own data: the mirror's own sample set, made for this mirror, and the subjects held in the network's databases. The scoring rule is the mirror's own rule, stated in full in Section 2. General ideas about encyclopedias and information retrieval are described here in general terms; no outside source is quoted as the mirror's own method. Codes. Network.
